title: Community Organizing: The Fundamentals
description: Community organizing — the systematic building of people-power — rests on the fundamentals: the one-on-ones (the relational meetings — the hundreds; the interests discovered; the leaders identified), the issue campaigns (the winnable — the specific; the researched; the escalated), the leadership development (the never do for others — the organized; the trained; the positioned), and the organization (the dues-paying members — the independent; the democratic — the owned). The traditions: the Alinsky (the Industrial Areas Foundation — the congregation-based; the confrontation), the ACORN (the membership-based; the direct action), the PICO (the faith-based; the moral voice), and the electoral (the voter engagement). The disciplines: the power analysis (the mapped), the winnable issues (the victories — the power built), and the independence (the dues — the agenda owned). The principle: the organizing builds the people’s power — the listened, the led, the won.
key_points: Never do for others what they can do
how_it_works: Listen via one-on-ones, recruit members, develop leaders, pick winnable issues, campaign, win.

title: The Congregation-Based Model (IAF Tradition)
description: Congregation-based organizing — the Industrial Areas Foundation tradition — builds power through faith communities: the institutions (the congregations — the dues-paying members; the organized; the moral voice), the leaders (the clergy and lay — the trained; the public), the issues (the family — the broadly felt; the winnable), and the actions (the accountability sessions — the public officials faced; the turnout — the demonstrated). The disciplines: the relational (the one-on-ones — the trust), the nonpartisan (the issues — the not the parties; the officials of all stripes — the held accountable), and the independent (the dues — the agenda). The strengths: the moral authority (the faith voice), the institutional durability (the congregations — the enduring), and the diversity (the multi-faith — the united). The principle: the organized faith is the community’s conscience with power.
how_it_works: Organize congregations, develop clergy/lay leaders, pick family issues, hold accountability sessions.

title: Mutual Aid Networks
description: Mutual aid — the community’s self-help systems — organizes: the needs and offers (the matched — the spreadsheets, the hotlines, the apps; the dignity — the no-means-testing), the pods (the neighborhood — the small; the trusted), the coordination (the dispatchers — the volunteers; the protocols — the clear), and the principles (the solidarity not charity — the horizontal; the everyone gives, everyone receives). The forms: the crisis response (the pandemic pods — the disaster relief), the ongoing (the food distribution — the childcare co-ops; the sustained), and the infrastructure (the community fridges — the free stores). The disciplines: the accessibility (the low-barrier — the multilingual), the sustainability (the coordinators — the supported; the burnout — the watched), and the politics (the demands — the articulated; the charity — the transcended). The principle: the mutual aid is the community caring for itself — the solidarity organized.
key_points: Needs matched with offers; no means-testing
how_it_works: Map needs and offers, form pods, coordinate dispatch, sustain coordinators, articulate demands.

title: The Community Fridge and Free Store
t: The Community Fridge and Free Store
description: Community fridges and free stores — the hyperlocal mutual aid infrastructure — run: the setup (the location — the hosted; the fridge — the stocked; the agreements — the food safety), the stocking (the volunteers — the scheduled; the donors — the grocery, the restaurant, the garden; the consistency), the maintenance (the cleaning — the temperature — the monitored), and the community (the norms — the take-what-you-need; the respect — the maintained). The disciplines: the host relationship (the business or faith host — the nurtured), the food safety (the standards — the honored), and the volunteer pipeline (the sustained). The strengths: the 24/7 access (the dignity — the no-hours), the visibility (the community’s care — the seen), and the simplicity (the low-cost). The principle: the fridge is the community’s open hand — the stocked, the clean, the welcoming.
how_it_works: Secure hosts, stock consistently, maintain safely, nurture norms, sustain volunteers.

title: The Neighborhood Association
description: Neighborhood associations — the block-level organizations — run: the boundaries (the defined — the known), the membership (the residents — the recruited; the dues — the modest), the meetings (the regular — the welcoming; the agenda — the issues plus the social), the issues (the safety — the development — the services — the advocated), and the community (the events — the block parties; the communication — the listserv, the newsletter). The disciplines: the inclusivity (the renters — the welcomed; the diversity — the reflected; the newcomers — the invited), the effectiveness (the issues — the won; the officials — the engaged), and the succession (the leaders — the rotated). The failure: the NIMBY capture — the exclusionary, the anti-change. The principle: the neighborhood association is the block’s voice — the inclusive, the effective, the welcoming.
how_it_works: Define boundaries, recruit inclusively, meet regularly, advocate effectively, socialize, rotate leaders.

title: Tenant Organizing
description: Tenant organizing — the renters’ power — builds: the building committees (the organized — the leaders; the demands — the specific: the repairs, the harassment, the rent), the associations (the multi-building — the united), the campaigns (the landlord — the pressured; the city — the lobbied; the courts — the used), and the wins (the repairs made — the harassment stopped — the rents stabilized — the ownership transferred where apt). The legal: the tenant rights (the known — the taught; the lawyers — the allied), the retaliation protection (the documented), and the organizing rights (the protected). The disciplines: the leadership (the tenants — the led; the organizers — the supporting), the escalation (the graduated — the strategic), and the sustainability (the dues — the independent). The principle: the tenants’ power is the organized building — the led by tenants, the won collectively.
how_it_works: Organize buildings, develop tenant leaders, make specific demands, escalate, win, sustain.

title: Faith-Based Community Development

The strengths: the moral voice (the trusted), the institutional base (the buildings — the people — the enduring), and the holistic (the spiritual plus the material). The principle: the faith in action — the community built, the justice sought, the people served.
key_points: Church CDCs building housing and businesses

title: The Mosque/Church/Synagogue as Community Hub
description: Houses of worship as community hubs — the open-door — host: the services (the food pantries — the clinics — the legal aid — the community’s), the gathering (the meetings — the events — the neutral ground), the youth (the programs — the mentoring — the safe space), and the crisis (the shelter — the disaster response — the refuge). The disciplines: the welcome (the all-faiths — the no-faiths — the served), the boundaries (the worship — the distinct; the proselytizing — the absent in services), and the partnerships (the secular — the allied). The strengths: the trust (the community’s), the space (the available), and the volunteers (the motivated). The principle: the house of worship’s doors open outward — the community’s hub, the all welcomed.
key_points: Services hosted: food, clinic, legal aid
Neutral ground for meetings and events
how_it_works: Open space, host services, welcome all, partner secularly, maintain boundaries.

title: Community Coalitions That Work
description: Community coalitions — the neighborhood alliances — work when: the shared stake (the issue — the affecting all; the win — the shared), the table (the organizations — the representative; the residents — the centered), the structure (the light — the facilitated; the decisions — the clear), and the action (the campaign — the joint; the wins — the shared). The disciplines: the resident power (the centered — the not the professionals’; the leadership — the developed), the equity (the small orgs — the voiced; the large — the resourced-sharing), and the coordination (the funded — the staffed). The failure: the professionals’ coalition — the residents as the backdrop. The principle: the coalition is the community’s united front — the resident-led, the equitably structured, the actively coordinated.
how_it_works: Convene around shared stake, center residents, structure lightly, fund coordination, campaign jointly.

title: Grassroots Fundraising
description: Grassroots fundraising — the many-small-donors — builds: the base (the supporters — the many; the list — the grown), the asks (the frequent — the specific; the story-driven — the compelling), the channels (the email — the segmented; the social — the peer-to-peer; the events — the house parties; the text — the mobile), and the sustenance (the monthly — the promoted; the upgraded — the mid-level identified). The disciplines: the testing (the A/B — the learned), the thanking (the immediate — the personal-feeling), and the independence (the agenda — the donor-base-owned; the no-single-funder capture). The strengths: the independence (the people-funded), the resilience (the many — the shock-absorbing), and the engagement (the donors — the activated). The principle: the grassroots-funded is the people-powered — the many small gifts, the independence, the movement.
key_points: Many small donors; list grown deliberately
Monthly sustainers; independence from big funders
how_it_works: Grow the list, ask frequently with stories, test channels, convert to monthly, guard independence.

title: Community Leadership Development
description: Community leadership development — the pipeline — builds: the identification (the natural leaders — the spotted in one-on-ones; the asked), the training (the skills — the one-on-ones, the meetings, the campaigns, the negotiation — the taught; the political education — the analyzed), the practice (the roles — the real; the mentored — the supported), and the positioning (the public — the visible; the boards — the appointed; the office — the run for). The disciplines: the never-do-for (the organized — the empowered), the diversity (the reflective — the community’s), and the sustainability (the burned-out — the prevented; the paid — the where possible). The principle: the community’s leaders are grown, not found — the pipeline is the power’s future.
how_it_works: Identify via one-on-ones, train systematically, give real roles, mentor, position publicly.

title: Youth Leadership Development
description: Youth leadership — the next generation — develops: the recruitment (the schools — the community; the invited — the welcomed), the training (the organizing skills — the campaign; the life skills — the professional; the political — the analyzed), the campaigns (the youth issues — the school discipline, the policing, the jobs — the won), and the pathways (the jobs — the internships; the college — the supported; the organizing careers — the offered). The disciplines: the youth-led (the adults — the supporting, not the directing), the safety (the protected), and the joy (the culture — the built). The strengths: the energy (the unstoppable), the moral clarity (the compelling), and the future (the pipeline). The principle: the youth are the movement’s present, not just its future — the led by youth, the supported by adults.
key_points: Train organizing, life, and political skills
how_it_works: Recruit youth, train comprehensively, support youth-led campaigns, build pathways, keep joyful.

title: Sustaining Community Organizations
description: Sustainability — the long-term survival — requires: the funding (the diversified — the dues, the grassroots, the grants, the earned — the resilient mix), the leadership (the pipelined — the renewed; the burned-out — the prevented), the relevance (the issues — the current; the community — the served as it changes), and the infrastructure (the systems — the documented; the knowledge — the transferred). The disciplines: the reserves (the 3–6 months — the buffered), the succession (the planned — the every key role), and the adaptation (the evaluated — the evolved). The failure: the founder-dependent, the funder-dependent, the issue-frozen — the unsustained. The principle: the sustained organization outlives its founders, its funders, and its first issues — the diversified, the pipelined, the adaptive.
how_it_works: Diversify funding, pipeline leaders, track relevance, document systems, build reserves, adapt.

title: The Community Land Trust
description: Community land trusts — the permanent affordability — work: the model (the trust owns the land — the residents own the homes; the ground lease — the 99-year; the resale formula — the affordability preserved), the governance (the tripartite board — the residents, the community, the public — the balanced), the development (the housing built — the rehabbed; the stewarded), and the funding (the public — the philanthropic; the earned — the lease fees). The strengths: the permanent affordability (the removed from speculation), the community control (the governed), and the wealth-building (the limited-equity — the residents’). The disciplines: the stewardship (the monitored — the enforced), the education (the buyers — the prepared), and the scale (the portfolio — the grown). The principle: the land held in trust for the community — the affordability permanent, the community in control.
key_points: Trust owns land; residents own homes; 99-year leases
how_it_works: Acquire land, develop housing, sell homes with resale formulas, govern tripartitely, steward permanently.

The models: the Evergreen (the Cleveland — the anchor-institution linked), the Mondragon-inspired (the networked), and the grassroots (the small — the many). The disciplines: the business rigor (the competitive), the democratic (the owned), and the patience (the built over decades). The principle: the community’s wealth owned by the community — the economics of the people.
key_points: Worker co-ops incubated; community loan funds
how_it_works: Incubate co-ops, capitalize locally, link anchors, educate, build patiently.

The forms: the identity-based (the shared — the focused), the place-based (the neighborhood — the local), and the hosted (the community foundation — the infrastructure). The strengths: the democratized giving (the everyone’s a philanthropist), the learning (the engaged), and the leverage (the pooled — the impactful). The disciplines: the participation (the engaged — the retained), the learning (the real — the not the tourism), and the equity (the community-voiced — the grantees centered). The principle: the giving circle is the philanthropy of the people — the pooled, the learned, the granted democratically.

The disciplines: the inclusive coalition (the affected — the centered), the legal (the binding — the enforceable, not the promised), and the monitoring (the ongoing — the funded). The failure: the handshake CBA — the promised, the unenforced. The principle: the development’s benefits shared with the community — the negotiated, the binding, the enforced.
key_points: Specific measurable demands: jobs, housing, environment

The disciplines: the equity (the marginalized — the centered), the deliberation (the informed — the discussed), and the follow-through (the implemented — the trusted). The strengths: the democracy (the direct), the equity (the redirected spending), and the engagement (the activated). The principle: the people’s money, the people’s decisions — the budgeted participatorily.
how_it_works: Allocate pot, outreach inclusively, develop proposals, vote accessibly, implement transparently.

The principle: the organizer is the leader-developer — the craft of building power through people.

Never do for others; develop leaders
